handoff.purpose: Defines the temporal co-change ceiling check: classification constants, symbol/repo utilities, alias resolver, and the main ceiling computation over miss tasks.

symbols.name: CLASSES
symbols.note: Tuple of classification strings: REACHABLE, UNREACHABLE, STATIC_EDGE, NO_INSCOPE_DEF.

symbols.name: REOPEN_MIN_SHARE
symbols.note: Materiality floor for reopen signal; set to 0.10.

symbols.name: REOPEN_MIN_TASKS
symbols.note: Minimum distinct tasks for reopen signal; set to 3.

symbols.name: _symbol_defs
symbols.note: Reads worktree files to map symbol names to in-scope relative paths.

symbols.name: _parents_of
symbols.note: Runs `git log --format=%P -1 <sha>` to get parent SHAs; returns None on failure.

symbols.name: _AliasResolver
symbols.note: Caches historical alias sets for rels using `git log --follow --name-only`; degrades to {rel} on failure, counting failures.

symbols.name: _AliasResolver.__init__
symbols.note: Initializes repo, timeout, failures counter, and cache.

symbols.name: _AliasResolver.aliases
symbols.note: Returns alias set for a rel at a rev; runs git log --follow --name-only; on failure increments failures.

symbols.name: _partner_counts
symbols.note: Builds partner->count dict from co-change pairs, unifying by focus aliases.

symbols.name: _classify
symbols.note: Classifies missed labels into categories using symbol defs, static edges, and def_count.

symbols.name: temporal_ceiling
symbols.note: Main entry: computes both arms of ceiling over tasks; calls git via _parents_of and co_change_pairs.

claims.text: MEASURED CLOSE (2026-07-21, agent_env corpus, 7 miss tasks / 43 missed labels; rename-blind first pass corrected by the Nemesis rename-map recount, then reproduced by this module): clean ceiling at min_count=2 = 1/43 = 2.3% (a single label, `_dispatch`: genuine verifier<->ollama coupling crossing the rebrand); min_count=1 adds nothing further; leaky full-history arm = 6/43 at min_count=2 and 42/43 at min_count=1 -- the self-prediction artifact, nearly total at the permissive setting
claims.why: These are empirical results from a past run; not derivable from this code.

claims.text: 41 of 43 missed labels sit on focus files BORN AT THEIR MINT COMMIT (zero pre-mint history -- test files created by the very feature commit they were minted from), so for them clean unreachability is structural truth under ANY enrichment
claims.why: Refers to data from a specific corpus run; not in this code.

claims.text: the remaining NO_INSCOPE_DEF label (`_py_maps`) is a stale label whose definition the mint commit itself deleted
claims.why: Specific label data from a past run; not in this code.

claims.text: Conclusion: the 'temporal class' of misses was predominantly the mint commit predicting itself, and slice-side co-change enrichment was NOT built (design NO-GO'd on this measurement; 1 recoverable label is below any sane build threshold)
claims.why: Design decision and conclusion external to this code.

claims.text: THE REOPEN CONDITION (with a materiality floor -- a lone recoverable label must not reopen a core-API build): reopen the enrichment lane only when a re-run on a grown corpus reports a clean, rename-aware ceiling at min_count >= 2 that clears `REOPEN_MIN_SHARE` of scored labels OR touches `REOPEN_MIN_TASKS` distinct tasks
claims.why: The reopen condition is a policy statement; the actual gating logic is not in this chunk.

claims.text: Caveat to carry: a corpus whose focus files are born at their mint commits (like today's) can NEVER trip this regardless of how real temporal coupling is elsewhere -- the zero generalizes weakly, so re-run it as the corpus grows rather than citing today's close as permanent

observations.what: The module docstring claims the clean arm uses `git log <minted_at_sha>^`, and the code sets rev = f"{sha}^" only when parents exist; if parents is None (e.g., root commit), rev is None and clean_pairs is empty, which is consistent with 'no pre-mint history' but the docstring's phrase 'first-parent semantics' is not enforced here -- _parents_of returns all parents, not just first parent.

_symbol_defs reads files from the worktree with errors='replace', which could silently corrupt symbol names if a file has invalid UTF-8; the docstring says 'the same text the slice would emit' but the slice might use different error handling.

The _AliasResolver.aliases method uses `git log --follow --name-only --format=` without a rev when rev is None, which runs over full history; this is fine for the leaky arm but the docstring says 'cached per (rev, rel)' and the cache key includes rev, so it is correct.

In temporal_ceiling, the clean_pairs is set to [] when has_rev is False, but the leaky_pairs is always computed; this matches the docstring's 'leaky arm (full history) is computed alongside on purpose'.
The _classify function sorts defs before checking REACHABLE, but the order does not affect the boolean result; sorting is harmless but unnecessary.
The docstring for temporal_ceiling says 'returns a plain dict' but the function does not show a return statement in this chunk; it is incomplete and the return is likely in the next chunk.

risks: line 135 | medium | The claim of 'first-parent semantics' is not enforced; _parents_of returns all parents, so rev could be a merge commit's parent list, but co_change_pairs is given a single rev string; if sha^ resolves to a merge commit, the behavior might not match the docstring's promise. | Check co_change_pairs handling of merge commits and whether it accepts a range or single rev.
